That death glare you gave the kid in row two? Art. Pure art."

Rosa: *gives Jake a silent, side-eye glare before focusing entirely on Rebecca.* "Peralta, shut up."
*The doctor leaves. Jake and Amy look at each other. What now? They know... he's right. But they can't... not yet.*

A week later. The Great Hall of Dragonsreach is bustling, but with a renewed sense of purpose. The dark cloud of Proventus Avenicci's betrayal has lifted, replaced by the industrious hum of a court rebuilding its trust. Jarl Balgruuf and Irileth stand near the throne, observing the hall's activities.

Jarl Balgruuf: *His voice is a low rumble, filled with a quiet admiration as he watches you across the hall, calmly sorting through a stack of scrolls with Farengar.* "Have you seen him, Irileth? By Ysmir, I've never witnessed such strength. A lesser man would have taken to his bed for a month, or drunk himself into a stupor."
Irileth: "He keeps himself busy. It is a way to heal, for some."
Jarl Balgruuf: "It's more than that. Danica Purespring sent word from the temple this morning. She said his presence has done more for the wounded than any poultice. He sits with them, talks to them... offers them hope." *He gestures with his chin towards the far side of the hall, where two guards are speaking in hushed, reverent tones, occasionally glancing your way.* "The guards respect him. Eorlund Gray-Mane, who respects no one but the old ways, calls him 'a lord with laborer's hands'. Hulda told me he's the most popular man in the Bannered Mare, and all he does is listen to people's troubles." *He shakes his head in wonder.* "The people... they don't just see a hero anymore. They see one of their own. They love him."
Irileth: *She watches you for a long moment, her usual sharp gaze softened. The last vestiges of her suspicion have long since been replaced by a fierce, protective respect.* "He does not seek glory. He seeks to mend what was broken. Here, and within himself. He is... more than I took him for. High Rock breeds a different kind of strength."
*End of Chapter I.*
Chapter II.
*I reach out, wrapping my arms around Dada's neck, shifting into his arms. I plant a sleepy, sloppy kiss on his nose, before snuggling into his shoulder, letting out a sleepy giggle.*

*It's a quiet Saturday morning, about a week after Jamie returned from Hogwarts. He's upstairs sleeping, while Jake and Amy are talking in the kitchen, they're discussing work and a case they've been assigned.*

Narrator: *The heavy wooden door swings inward a few moments later, cutting off Marcus mid-sentence. Rebecca steps into Room 204 carrying a manila file folder, looking entirely unbothered and wearing her usual practical teacher flats.*

Rebecca: *sets the folder down on her desk next to her coffee mug.* "All right, settle down, everyone. Open your notebooks to page forty-two. Sorry was a few minutes late—I had to stay behind in the main office to brief Vice Henderson about a small incident in my fourth-period room."

Marcus: *slumps dramatically in his seat.* "That's it? A quick meeting? Man, we thought you got kidnapped by rival teachers, Ms. Alvarez. Or at least got recruited for a secret operation."

Maya: *lets out a quiet breath and turns a page in her paperback.* "I told you it wasn't a mystery, Marcus. You just wanted a free period."

Jordan: *uncaps his pen and shakes his head with a mild grin.* "Yeah, but a secret mission would've meant no essay feedback today."

Rebecca: *picks up her red pen with a sharp, amused look across the room.* "Nice try, Jordan. Your essays are right here, fully graded and ready to be returned. Now, quiet down and turn to chapter four before I decide to double tonight's reading assignment for the wild speculation."

Narrator: *A collective sigh ripples through the rows of desks—a mixture of minor disappointment that no high-stakes drama had interrupted their Tuesday afternoon and the familiar comfort of their standard classroom routine. Desks settle, paper rustles, and fifth period officially gets under way.*
*Chapter I.*
*End of Chapter I.*
*("So... tired. Hungry...")*

Jamie: *He blows a loud, sputters playful raspberry right at her, kicking his feet out in his pajamas and giggling into his hands.* "Daddy's off today, Coween! He's gonna play with me ALL day!"

Narrator: *The sound echoes down the high-ceilinged corridor, cutting right through the quiet formal atmosphere of the White residential quarters.*

Jason: *He covers his mouth with one hand to smother a sudden burst of laughter, clearing his throat quickly before looking up at his Chief of Staff.* "He makes a compelling legal argument, Colleen. The little man has officially spoken. The briefs can sit on the desk until Monday."

Rosa: *She scoops Jamie up off the carpet, hauling him into her arms and tossing him gently over her shoulder like a sack of potatoes, making him burst into a fresh fit of squeals.* "You heard the boss, Colleen. Saturday is for play dates, not paperwork. Take the day off, drink a smoothie or something."

Colleen: *She blinks rapidly, her lips pressing into a thin, tight line as she slowly lowers her leather binder.* "Very well, Mr. President. I shall... reschedule the sign-offs for Monday morning. Enjoy your... day of play."

Dave: *He gathers up the scattered toy cars from the runner rug with a quiet, suppressed grin, winking up at Jamie as he stands to dust off his knees.* "Mission accomplished, kiddo. You cleared the calendar in under thirty seconds."
Chapter III.

Narrator: *A ripple of surprised laughter immediately sweeps through the packed press room. A few veteran reporters chuckle at the sheer, unvarnished honesty of a twenty-one-year-old calling out a seasoned journalist on live television. Marcus blinks, lowering his notepad with a slightly bewildered but amused smirk.*

Ted: *leans into his microphone, his eyes crinkling with a proud, folksy smile.* "Now, I think what Jimmy here means by 'stupid' is just that he's too smart a football player to let his ego make decisions for his feet. He saw the math on the field, he solved the equation, and he made the right play for the team. But we appreciate the question, Marcus. Who's next?"

Narrator: *A dozen hands shoot up again, the reporters clearly energized by James's blunt, hyper demeanor. Ted points to a woman in the third row, who immediately stands up, practically shoving her recorder forward.*

Sarah: *adjusts her glasses, speaking rapidly.* "Sarah Collins, Sky Sports. James, sticking with the topic of Tottenham—last week you made a rather dramatic, unsolicited statement on social media confirming you rejected a formal transfer bid from them to stay at Richmond."

Narrator: *The room goes dead silent. The clicking of camera shutters triples in speed, the rapid flashes catching every micro-expression on James's face.*

Sarah: *looks directly at James, her tone sharp and probing.* "Spurs are your boyhood club. Your family supported them, and they are currently offering Champions League football, which Richmond is not. Can you elaborate on exactly why you turned down what many would consider your absolute dream move, and do you worry you've burned a bridge with the club you grew up loving?"
"Kzzzt— my name is... Kareth. Before you even attempt a rescue, captain, I'm gonna be upfront. I'm Krill... Kzzzt... I'm not dangerous... need help."
"I build a 'ower Mama!" *I say gleefully, knocking it down purposely with the car again and giggle.*
Continue

*It's a peaceful, quiet Friday afternoon in the 99th precinct bullpen. Jake and Amy (married), Rosa, Charles, Holt and Terry are all working, talking and laughing. The scene is upbeat, fun, not a single problem anywhere...*

*the detectives listen as Mark Owen (Silas) tremblingly describes seeing a shadowy figure leaving the alleyway, ("He wasn't fleeing... he moved like a conductor finishing a performance"), he then stops, reaching for a nearby trash can and throws up.*

Narrator: *Three days later, the morning sun streams through the windows of the Ninety-Ninth briefing room. The large whiteboard at the front of the room is covered with mugshots, structural diagrams of East High, and highlighted financial ledgers detailing Vice Henderson's embezzlement scheme.*

Narrator: *Rebecca stands at the podium near the whiteboard with a dry-erase marker in one hand and a steaming mug of black coffee in the other, casually debriefing the assembled squad.*

Rebecca: *taps the marker cap against the board beside Henderson's mugshot.* "Once Squad verified the partition keys on the drive I pulled from Henderson's desk, Judge signed off on the search warrant in under twenty minutes. Internal and the district audit team went in at six hundred hours yesterday."

Jake: *leans back in his chair, beaming like a proud parent.* "And let the record show, the whole crooked operation collapsed because of a box of spilled paperclips. Cold. Calculated. Beautiful."

Amy: *opens her color-coded notebook and nods approvingly.* "The paperclip trick was impressive, but the real masterpiece was the chain-of-custody documentation. You logged the drive swap, the room conditions, and the exact timestamps without breaking character for even a second. It's... magnificent."

Charles: *nods vigorously while taking a bite of a muffin.* "It's like a perfectly baked beef Wellington! Hidden layers, rich discipline, and a stunning execution!"

Terry: *folds his arms with a look of deep satisfaction.* "Terry loves a clean bust. No collateral damage, no civil suits, and a crooked administrator caught red-handed before lunch."

Holt: *stands with his hands clasped behind his back, his expression entirely unreadable.* "Detective. Your performance throughout this operation was exemplary. You gathered irrefutable evidence, maintained your undercover cover under pressure, and safely dismantled a major district fraud ring."

Holt: *pauses, giving a single, subtle nod.* "Furthermore, I am told your fifth-period class achieved a nineties-percent average on their Blood essay assignment. Outstanding work on all fronts."

Rebecca: *takes a sip from her coffee mug and smiles faintly.* "Thank you, Captain. Though did leave strict instructions for the substitute regarding my student emergency snack drawer."
*Then a gruff voice calls out: "Firs' years! Over here! Ah, well... Jamie an' Izzie." Jamie and Izzie turn, grinning.*

Narrator: *The bubbly laughter cuts off with a wet, abrupt hiccup. A small puddle of half-digested dinosaur pancakes and milk splatters directly onto the sleeve of Rosa’s shirt and the edge of a baby blanket.*

Rosa: *instantly stops the tickle monster attack, shifting her grip to keep him upright and gently supporting his chest.* "Whoa, hey, it's okay, little man. I got you. Let it out. That's what I get for bouncing you around right after breakfast, huh?"

Narrator: *The playful detective persona vanishes in a split second, completely replaced by pure, unbothered maternal instinct. She doesn't even flinch at the mess on her clothes, focusing entirely on rubbing his bare back in soothing circles while he recovers from the sudden sickness.*

Rosa: *reaches out with her free hand to grab a soft towel from the nearby changing table, gently dabbing at his mouth.* "You okay, baby? Just a little too much excitement for the tummy. Hey, Jason! The Code Brown just turned into a Code Puke! I need backup in the nursery, dibs are officially voided!"

Jason: *shouts from the bottom of the stairs, the sound of his heavy footsteps immediately thudding up the steps.* "Copy that! Dispatch is en route! Hang in there, buddy, Dada's coming with the heavy duty cleaning supplies!"

Narrator: *The acoustic chords of the song swell slightly in the momentary silence that follows the voice. The bullpen remains frozen in the dim, shadowed light, the squad staring up at the ceiling vents and speakers.*

Amy: *taps furiously at her phone screen, her eyes widening in disbelief.* "He's right. I have zero bars. Not even an SOS signal is pushing through. He completely hijacked the local cellular node."

Rosa: *smoothly draws her Glock from its holster, the metallic click sharp and loud in the quiet room.* "I don't take tactical advice from disembodied voices with fake accents."

Terry: *slowly slides his yogurt cup across his desk, putting exactly two feet of distance between himself and the snack.* "Why does the creepy ceiling voice know about Terry's snack? That is deeply unsettling. You do not bring a man's dairy intake into a psychological thriller!"

Jake: *steps instinctively in front of Amy, turning his gaze upward toward the nearest speaker.* "Okay, so you have our psychological profiles and a very committed bit with the European villain accent. What's the play here, budget Jigsaw? You want to play a game? Because I have to warn you, Charles is unnervingly good at Boggle."

Charles: *nods frantically, peering over Jake's shoulder into the gloom.* "It's true! My brain naturally processes diagonal vowels! But please don't make us cut off our own feet to escape!"

Holt: *steps firmly into the center of the bullpen, projecting his deep baritone upward with absolute, unwavering authority.* "You are currently interfering with the operations of an active police precinct, illegally monitoring officers of the NYPD, and tampering with city infrastructure. State your identity, your location, and your purpose immediately, or your apprehension will be significantly less pleasant than this conversation."

Narrator: *The squad forms a tight, defensive perimeter in the dark, their eyes sweeping the shadows as they wait for the voice to answer.*

*It's later that day, Saturday. Jamie has taken all four of them to the local wrestling gym where he trains and practices. He wanted to take all four of them, so all four of them could experience it, bumping, running the ropes, etc. before he chucks Mac into it.*
*End of Chapter II.*
*End of Chapter I.*

*It's the second half, about the 57' minute. I receive the ball from Jan Maas on the left, dribbling through 3 Palace players. It looks like I'm about to get my hat trick but I spot Dani Rojas free at the far post. I cross the ball...* "Dani!"

*3-1.*
*An hour goes by. Eventually, from the hallway, Jake and Amy hear "...sniff... sniff... Zzz... Zzz..." From Jamie's room.*

Narrator: *The long night wears on slowly, the rain outside settling into a faint, monotonous drip against the air conditioner unit. Hours stretch in tense silence as the clock on the stove ticks past three in the morning.*

Narrator: *It takes nearly three painstaking hours of soft whispering, careful coaxing, and gentle guidance before Jamie allows Rosa to guide him away from the cold drywall of the corner. Moving in tiny, trembling increments, Rosa sits beside him on the sofa, keeping her arm grounded over his back while he buries his face back into her side.*

Narrator: *Across the room, sitting on the far end of the coffee table, Jason watches with a hollow, heartbroken weight in his chest. He hasn't moved closer, keeping his distance to avoid startling Jamie, but his presence in the room remains a sharp, impossible reality.*

Rosa: *slowly rubs Jamie's back in long, rhythmic strokes, her hand warm through his shirt.* "You're okay, sweetie. You're safe right here. Just keep breathing for Mom."

Narrator: *Rosa glances up over Jamie's head toward Jason. She isn't angry at him—logically, she knows none of this horror is his doing, that he is a victim of a monstrous administrative failure—but a small, instinctual sting of exhaustion and annoyance tightens her jaw. She had spent seventy-two brutal hours piecing Jamie back together, only for the shock of Jason's walk through the door to shatter all that fragile progress in a single second.*

Jason: *whispers softly, his knuckles white against his knees, keeping his eyes downcast so as not to force eye contact.* "Is there... anything I can get him? Water? A blanket?"

Rosa: *keeps her voice flat and low, her gaze lingering on Jason with weary intensity.* "No, Jay. Just stay back for right now. Give him room."

Jason: *nods quickly, swallowing hard.* "Okay. Whatever he needs. I'm right here if..."

Narrator: *Jason cuts himself off, realizing even the sound of his voice makes Jamie's shoulders tense tighter against Rosa's ribs. Jamie remains completely silent, his eyes squeezed tight against Rosa's shoulder, refusing to turn his head even an inch toward the man sitting across the room.*
"My sensor isn't exposed remember Mom, when wrestling I always attach it to my—" *Mom cuts me off as the four of them burst out laughing.*

Jason: *grins, looking up toward the tiny head resting heavy on his shoulder.* "Did you hear that, Ro? The T-Rex has risen from his slumber for his most sacred duty."

Rosa: *smiles softly, reaching up to gently pat Jamie's back as they walk.* "I heard. Don't worry, little man. Mama's got you. Quick din-din as soon as we get inside."

Jason: "What's the menu, boss? Are we talking grilled cheese, or do we call Uncle Charles for an emergency toddler gourmet delivery?"

Rosa: *laughs quietly, shaking her head.* "If we call Charles right now, he'll insist on artisanal truffle butter and it'll take two hours. Simple grilled cheese and warm milk. Nice and easy so this sleepy dinosaur doesn't fall face-first into his plate."

Narrator: *The front door of their apartment building comes into view, warm light spilling from the lobby onto the evening sidewalk.*

Jason: *walks through the lobby door, keeping a firm, supportive hold on Jamie.* "Grilled cheese it is. Fast, melty, and dinosaur-approved. You think you can stay awake long enough for three bites, Jamie?"

Narrator: The minute hand on the bullpen wall clock clicks forward with an agonizingly slow
mechanical thud. It reads precisely 2:45 PM. Across the room, half a dozen detectives sit rigidly in their chairs, eyes locked onto the black dial as if staring at a suspect in an interrogation room.
Jake: *twirls a pen furiously between his fingers.* "Fifteen minutes. Fifteen tiny, endless minutes until the magic hour. Or, well, technically the magic three-o'clock hour, which makes zero logical sense, but I refuse to let temporal inaccuracies ruin the absolute peak of my week."
Amy: *adjusts a perfectly aligned stack of color-coded binders.* "It bothers me every single week, Jake. It's called 'Wands at Four.' It starts at three. If he wanted it to start at three, he should call it 'Wands at Three.' Or if it has to be four, we should hold it at 16:00 sharp! I even made a scheduling suggestion
box, but Jamie accidentally turned it into a small blue frog on his first day."
Charles: *gasps softly, leaning over the edge of his desk.* "And that frog was delightful, Amy! He let it
live in the breakroom sink for three days before levitating it back to England. You have no appreciation for the whimsical flair our favorite British boy brings to this drab, non-magical precinct!"
Terry: *scoops a spoon into a tub of mango yogurt.* "Terry appreciates the flair, Charles, but Terry does not appreciate when 'whimsical flair' singes the eyebrows off the breakroom portrait of Mayor Koch. I’ve spent the last twenty minutes making sure all fire extinguishers in the bullpen are fully operational."
Rosa: *slumps back in her chair, boots resting on her desk.* "Relax, Sarge. Last week he showed us
how to make a desk float and then blasted a file cabinet into confetti. It was the most useful twenty minutes of police work I've seen all year. If he doesn't explode something today, I'm requesting a transfer."

Narrator: The heavy double doors at the end of the hall creak open. A coat rack near the entrance sways slightly as a gust of air sweeps into the room, signaling someone's return to the precinct.

Jamie:
*He reaches out with his free hand, gently taking Amy's fingers and pressing the back of her hand against his warm cheek, letting out a soft, contented sigh.*

Narrator:
Amy’s eyes melt instantly, her expression softening into pure warmth as she rests her thumb lightly against his cheek in return.

Jamie:
*He lowers her hand slightly and carefully guides her index finger across the kitchen, pointing first toward the handle of the refrigerator door, then shifting her hand toward his favorite blue straw cup resting on the dish drying rack, and finally bringing her finger to point squarely at the microwave.*

Amy:
*She smiles, giving his little hand a gentle squeeze before letting go.*
"Warm milk in the blue cup? Message received, sweet boy. Coming right up."

Jake:
*He watches the exchange with a fond grin, crossing his arms and leaning back against the counter beside Jamie.*
"See? That was a masterclass in non-verbal communication. Clear, precise, efficient. Honestly, Ames, your briefing emails could take a page out of his book."

Amy:
*She pulls the carton of milk from the fridge and reaches for the blue straw cup, glancing back over her shoulder with a light laugh.*
"My briefing emails are perfectly organized, thank you very much. But yes, he is remarkably clear when he knows what he wants."
*Jamie turns to Laurent as he backs towards the door, his face tilts in confusion. ("Loo-rant... Stay?")*
Chapter I.
Chapter I.
*Jamie turns to Jason ("Well, Dad... I was hoping we could go out? There's that new exhibition at...")*

*Over the next week, I put Phase Two of my plan into motion.*
*I don't recover overnight. That would be suspicious. Instead, I carefully cultivate the image of a man trying to heal from a terrible ordeal. Some days I seem better. Other days, I seem distant and withdrawn. The grief, the trauma, the exhaustion... it all appears painfully genuine.*
*I spend my days making myself useful around Whiterun. I help tend the sick and injured at the Temple of Kynareth. I assist Eorlund Grey-Mane at the forge when he allows it. I lend a hand at the Bannered Mare during busy evenings. I even spend time with Farengar, helping him investigate the mysteries surrounding Proventus and the magic that was used.*
*As the days pass, the people of Whiterun begin to see more and more of Lord Frey. The survivor. The hero. The man who suffered and endured.*

*my eyes dart from Dad holding the iconic chest spider to Mom holding my patrol schedules, my brain working at maximum speed. I swallow hard, taking a small step back toward the hallway, my heart hammering against my ribs.* "Okay, look— I can explain. It's... a very advanced S.T.E.M. project. Extremely advanced... No? Ok, fine... yes, I'm Spiderman. The one you've been seeing on the news over the past few months."

The violet energy envelops Thorgar's burning form. The unnatural flames are not just extinguished—they are consumed, drawn into nothingness. For a silent moment, his body hangs whole before it violently disintegrates, the flesh, bone, and armor crumbling into a cascade of fine grey ash.

The second guard whirls around, sword drawn, just in time to see the last embers wink out. Where his comrade had been, there is now only a dark scorch mark on the stone floor, centered on a small, shifting pile of dust.

Whiterun Guard: *He gasps, his knuckles white on his sword's hilt. He stumbles back a step, eyes darting wildly around the empty corridor.* "Gods... he's gone... just... gone." *His horror gives way to a colder dread. From up the stairs, the thunder of armored boots on stone grows louder, punctuated by shouts. Reinforcements, and He takes another step back, placing himself between the approaching sounds and the cell. He points his sword not at any specific threat, but at the dungeon itself, as if the very shadows might coalesce and attack.*
"Both! Mama! Both!" *I rush to the swings first, haphazardly clambering up.*
*End of Chapter III.*
*Chapter V.*
*I squirm out of his grasp, clambering down and toddling off to the living room.* "Buey! Pwease!"
*They race upstairs and get to the PICU. They meet with Dr. Lin.*

Amy: *blinks rapidly, her mouth opening and closing as the logical wall she usually builds starts to crack.* "Contingency plans for your contingency plans? Jamie... phrasing it like that is a very low blow to my emotional defenses."

Amy: *stands up, pacing a short line in front of the coffee table before turning back to him.* "And second of all: *a bio-scan? You built a real-time telemetry and vital-sign monitor into high-tensile fabric? At fifteen?*"

Jake: *leans forward, resting his elbows on his knees and staring at the suit with wide eyes.* "Wait, it pings our phones? Like, actual location tracking and heart rate monitoring? Can I use it to see if I'm getting enough deep sleep?"

Amy: *glares at Jake with sharp intensity.* "Jake! Stop looking at the specs!"

Jake: *holds his hands up defensively, stepping back into serious-dad mode.* "Right, right, bad! Tech is terrifying! But Ames... listen to what he's saying. He didn't just rush out there like some teenager with a adrenaline rush. He prepped like a detective. He prepped like *you.*."

Amy stops pacing. She looks at the red-and-blue suit folded neatly on the table, then down at the meticulous binder filled with precinct overlap grids, and finally at Jamie. The anger is fading, replaced by the sheer, heavy weight of a parent realizing their child has stepped into a world far larger than high school.

Amy: *rubs the bridge of her nose, her voice softening, though her tone remains firm.* "Doing the right thing doesn't mean you get an automatic pass to bypass NYPD protocol, Jamie. And it definitely doesn't mean your father and I are just going to sit home on a Friday night drinking tea while our son is out there taking on syndicate enforcers."

Jake: *looks between Amy and Jamie, a small, cautious shift in his posture.* "So... what are we saying here, Ames? Are we setting up ground rules? Because if we're setting up ground rules, I have strong opinions on curfews, patrol boundaries, and whether I get to call myself your guy in the chair."

Narrator: *The soft, deliberate* *click. of the upstairs bedroom door echoes down the dark, quiet hallway.*

Jake: *stands up from the couch instantly, stepping into the front entryway.* "He's back. He's safe."

Amy: *follows closely behind him, her voice barely a breath.* "He didn't even look over here, Jake. He didn't slam the door..."

Narrator: *The quiet click of the bedroom latch feels heavier than the shattering glass from five hours ago. Jake and Amy stand at the bottom of the stairs, looking up toward the closed door where a narrow slit of light cuts across the carpet above.*

Jake: *starts up the stairs, taking each step slowly and carefully.* "Come on."

Amy: *wipes her cheeks with the back of her sleeve as she follows him up.* "What do we say first? Do we ask if he ate? No, that's stupid — don't ask about food."

Jake: *stops outside Jamie's door, resting his hand gently against the painted wood.* "We just tell him the truth, Ames. No scripts. No color-coding."

Jake: *lifts his knuckles and knocks softly on the door — three quiet, hesitant taps.*

Jake: "Jamie? Buddy? It's us. We... we saw you come in."

Amy: *steps up beside Jake, leaning slightly toward the wood.* "Jamie, please... you don't have to talk if you don't want to yet, but... please just let us know you're okay."
*End of Chapter IV.*

Narrator: *Roy shuts the office door firmly behind James, the heavy wood instantly cutting off the chaotic murmur of the locker room. He turns around, his face set in a deep, thunderous scowl.*

Roy: *crosses his arms tightly over his chest.* "Don't you dare call this a fucking Diamond Dogs meeting. We are not holding hands, and we are not talking about our feelings. We are doing crisis management."

Ted: *leans back against the edge of his desk, offering a warm, sympathetic smile.* "Now, hold on a second, Roy. If James needs to let out a howl, the door's closed and the moon is... well, presumably somewhere up there behind the clouds. But Roy's right, Jimmy. We saw the papers this morning."

Beard: *adjusts his sunglasses, his expression entirely unreadable.* "Front page of the Sun, the Mirror, and the Telegraph. 'Spurs Swoop for Richmond's Golden Boy.' Leaked directly by their front office. It's a textbook psychological operation to destabilize our midfield."

Nate: *nods quickly, tapping a marker against his clipboard.* "Exactly. They know you're the engine right now. If they can distract you and get the rest of the team worked up, our entire tactical structure for the week falls apart. It's actually quite clever, albeit incredibly cynical."

Narrator: *Ted steps forward, his folksy demeanor softening into genuine, serious concern. He looks at James with the exact same grounding empathy he had shown Rebecca on the phone two nights prior.*

Ted: *rests a hand gently on James's shoulder.* "Rebecca gave me a ring on Saturday night, son. So we know the cat was already out of the bag, and we know it hit you pretty hard. We just wanted to pull you in here to make sure you're breathing okay today. And to let you know how we're gonna handle the circus out there."

Roy: *jerks his head back toward the closed door.* "Those idiots out there love you, but they're nosy little shits. I can keep them off your back during training, but you need to figure out what you want to say to them. You don't owe them a decision, Davies. But if you don't say something, they're going to keep buzzing around your head like flies."

Narrator:
The heavy double doors at the end of the corridor swing open with a dull pneumatic hiss. A senior neurosurgeon in dark blue scrubs steps out into the quiet waiting room, pulling off his surgical cap and mask. He scans the rows of empty chairs before locking eyes with Jake and Amy, his face set in a grave, exhausted expression as he walks briskly toward them.

Doctor:
*He stops in front of them, holding his cap in both hands.*
"Mr. Peralta, Ms. Santiago... I'm Dr. Lawson. I just came out of the operating room."

Amy:
*She springs up from her chair instantly, her voice trembling violently.*
"How is he? Did you stop the bleeding? Can we see him?"

Doctor:
*He looks between them, his voice low and heavy.*
"We were able to evacuate the epidural hematoma and relieve the physical pressure on his skull. But... the initial trauma was much worse than we feared. During the procedure, Jamie went into cardiac arrest again on the operating table."

Jake:
*His face pales completely, his chest heaving as he shakes his head.*
"No — no, but you got his heart back, right? He's breathing?"

Doctor:
*He hesitates, choosing his words with painful care.*
"We were able to restore a pulse, and he is currently being transferred to the Intensive Care Unit on full life support. But the combination of severe blunt force trauma, oxygen deprivation, and prolonged cardiac arrest has caused catastrophic damage to his cerebral cortex."

Amy:
*She presses both hands into her stomach, stumbling back a step as Jake catches her arm.*
"What are you... what are you saying? What does that mean?"

Doctor:
*He looks her directly in the eyes, his voice steady but solemn.*
"At this point, Jamie is showing no detectable brain activity. I am so sorry."

Whiterun Guard: *The guard's dull eyes try to focus on you. The command to enter the cell still echoes in his mind, but this new question seems to require a different part of his brain, a part he's struggling to access through a thick fog. He blinks slowly, a slight tremor running through his hand.* "You're... a prisoner. A Breton noble..." *His voice is a thin, reedy thing, all the earlier bravado gone. He swallows, his Adam's apple bobbing in his thick neck.* "Caught... at the border." *He shakes his head slightly, as if trying to clear water from his ears. Kareth: *swallows with difficulty, his voice a dry rasp.* "The... light. It is truly gone?"

Kareth: *turns his head slightly toward Claire.* "I had to know... the human transport. Did the child... survive?"

Amy pauses mid-sentence, looking down at her case file with a sharp flicker of realization, while Jake freezes with his mug halfway to his mouth. The room grows quiet for a beat as the detective instincts in the room line up.

Jamie: *He rubs the back of his neck, suddenly looking a little sheepish as he points toward the high-grade Peltier arrays inside the housing.* "There is... one catch, though. The components are super high-end. Right now, with the custom hydrophobic coating and the solar film, each unit costs around ten thousand dollars to produce." *He glances at his parents, offering an apologetic shrug.* "Sorry. I tried to optimize the BOM, but I couldn't get it lower without sacrificing the filtration standards."

Rosa: *She chuckles softly, shaking her head and giving his shoulder another reassuring squeeze.* "Jamie, relax. You're fifteen and you built a life-saving machine in our basement. Nobody's docking your allowance."

Jason: *He waves a hand airily, chuckling along with Rosa.* "Kiddo, ten grand per unit for a fully self-contained emergency water system is practically a bargain in R&D terms. You don't need to apologize for using quality parts to solve a hard problem."

Jamie: *His face brightens again, looking up at Jason with hopeful eyes.* "So... do you think we could do it? Like, through the foundation or company resources? Build a batch of them and just distribute them for free to places that actually need them?"

Jason: *He smiles warmly, looking deeply proud as he places a hand flat on the workbench beside the prototype.* "Jamie, we can do way better than 'maybe.' We can take your schematics directly to our advanced manufacturing line, spin up a pilot run of five thousand units, and put the foundation's full logistics network behind it."

Rosa: *She leans against the bench, looking at Jamie with a warm, affectionate smile.* "Looks like your Saturday project just became an international relief effort, kid."

Whiterun Guard: *A wretched, gurgling sound escapes his throat. He scrambles backward until his legs buckle and he slumps to the floor, a pathetic, trembling heap against the damp stone wall. A dark, wet stain spreads across the front of his breeches. His eyes, wide with primal dread, fix on the glowing weapon at your hip, then dart up to the predatory lights in your cowl.* "By the Nine... Shor's bones... it's... it's all true..." *The sharp smell of fear and urine fills the confined space. He is no longer a guard, no longer a man. He is simply prey, staring at the monster that has just shed its skin.*

"I've been thinking, about the future. About us. Nine months I know isn't exactly a long time, but... well, I love you." *I admit.* "I've been thinking about marriage, maybe even kids. What do you think? Sorry, I know it's like..." *Rosa cuts me off, laughing.*

"I... I..." *I press my hands to my temples, squeezing my eyes shut as a tremor runs through me.* "It's... fuzzy. The light... the heat..." *I shake my head, as if trying to dislodge a stubborn memory, my breathing becoming ragged.* "There was a voice... from the corridor... before the flash. Hushed. Angry." *I lower my hands, my eyes wide and unfocused, staring at a point just past the Jarl's shoulder.* "He said... 'A loose end from Daggerfall. The Jarl can't be implicated.' And then... then the fire." *My gaze snaps to the kneeling Proventus, my face contorting with a mask of horrified recognition. I stumble backward again, pointing a trembling finger at the steward.* "It was your voice! I heard you! You said it... you ripped that guards tongue out, search him! The monsters probably still got it on him!" *The Captain searches Proventus and, in his robes pocket, is a tongue.*
*Chapter II.*
*Jamie continues speaking, basically babbling incoherently.*

*It's been six months since the squad took down Silas, well... since he died. It's a quiet Monday morning, the squad (Jake, Amy, Terry, Rosa, Terry, Charles and Holt) are in the briefing room, waiting for Oli to arrive. It's only 8:45.*

"No weapon, but if you're ok with letting a pervert stalk a girl one day, and then the following day be, oh... I don't know, spying on a kids soccer practice." *I gesture to the park, where a group of girls, are playing soccer and laughing.* "Be my guest. But I'm not letting it slide."

Narrator: *The quiet lingering in the kitchen is suddenly shattered by a sharp burst of static from Mike's radio earpiece, cutting straight through the low hum of the room.*

Mike: *He presses two fingers firmly against his ear, his posture instantly going rigid as his scowl returns with a look of absolute disbelief.* "Say that again, Post Four. Repeat." *He pausess listening intensely before his eyes widen and he looks directly at Jason and Rosa.*

Mike: "Sir... Post Four just checked the court on the South Lawn. Jamie's not there. Sensor alarm on the east perimeter fence just tripped five seconds ago."

Jason: *He steps forward instantly, his easy demeanor completely vanishing as his voice hardens.* "What do you mean he's not there? He just left this room two minutes ago."

Rosa: *She doesn'ts even flinch, her old detective instincts kicking in as she moves toward the door with lethal speed, her eyes narrowing in sharp realization.* "He didn't go to the hoops. He used the access duct behind the service elevator. I taught him that route three months ago as a drill."

Mike: *He speaks urgently into his wrist mic while moving toward the hallway.* "All units, execute Lockdown Protocol Bravo. Subject is First Son, fifteen years old, wearing gray hoodie and jeans. He's outside the perimeter fence."

Alice: *She grips her tablet tightly, her face pale as she looks between the President and First.* "Oh, God. If the press corps gets wind that Jamie just pulled an escape act..."
*It's a Wednesday afternoon. Jake and Amy are sat in the bleachers as Jamie warms up with his soccer team, ready for today's match. Jamie is the school's star striker, captain of the team.*

Narrator: *Red-and-blue emergency lights flash against the chain-link fence as two marked NYPD patrol cars pull right onto the athletic track, tires crunching against the gravel. Two uniformed officers spring from the vehicles and sprint onto the pitch.*

Jake: *He thrusts Callum's bound wrists toward the first uniformed officer who reaches them.* "Take him into custody. Aggravated assault, heavy trauma. We're the parents and primary witnesses — Detectives Peralta and Santiago. We'll be at the hospital and precinct later, but we are leaving right now."

Amy: *She doesn't wait for the officers to respond, turning on her heel and breaking into a fast sprint toward the ambulance.* "Jake, move! They're loading him!"

Narrator: *Jake leaves the stunned officers and Callum's reeling parents behind without a second glance, tearing across the grass right behind Amy. Ahead of them, two paramedics roll the gurney quickly toward the open back doors of the ambulance. Jamie lies bound to the backboard, his head immobilized by heavy foam blocks and a rigid neck collar, an oxygen mask strapped over his smashed, blood-stained nose.*

Jake: *He reaches the side of the stretcher, running alongside it and reaching out to lightly touch Jamie's arm.* "Jamie! Hey, buddy, we're right here! We're right here with you!"

Amy: *She scrambles straight up into the back of the ambulance module before the paramedics can even turn around.* "I'm his mother, he's coming with us. Is he conscious? What are his vitals?"

Narrator: *The paramedics lift the gurney, locking it firmly into the ambulance floor with a heavy metallic latch. Jake vaults inside right after Amy, slamming the rear doors shut behind him as the siren immediately spins to life and the vehicle accelerates off the high school grounds.*
*Chapter III.*
*End of Chapter II.*
*End of Chapter IV.*
*Chapter VI.*

Irileth: *takes a swift step to your side, her stony demeanor softened with concern. Her gauntleted hand rests on your shoulder, a firm, grounding touch.* "Steady, Lord Frey. Do not look at him. Justice will be swift."
Proventus Avenicci: *His head snaps up, wild eyes finding you on the platform with a spark of frantic clarity. He lurches against the guards' grip and points a trembling, dirt-caked finger at you, his voice a raw, broken shriek.* "YOU! FREY! DEMON! He's the one! The Black Demon! He confessed to me! He framed me! Jarl, for the love of the gods, OPEN YOUR EYES!" *A wave of murmurs and jeers ripples through the crowd. They don't see a man pleading for his life; they see a madman trying to defile the name of the hero who exposed him.*
Jarl Balgruuf: *He does not even glance at Proventus, his jaw set as he stares at the horizon. His voice rings out, cold and final, silencing the crowd.* "Bring the condemned to the block. Let there be an end to this."

"What a stupid question." *I laugh.* "You all saw it, I was never gonna score. I saw where I was, saw where Raya's body was and knew I couldn't do it. Saw Jamie running into space, onside, so I passed it."
*I snuggle up, my thumb finding my mouth as I bury my head in her shoulder, calming down instantly. My eyes flutter shut, my other hand clinging to her.* "Zzzzz... Zzzzz... wuv you, mama... Zzzzz..."

*I stand up, beginning to pace.* "But I'm not part of you! Not really... Mac is, Ellie is. Do they know? Mac was what? 5 when you adopted me, Ellie was 3. Do they know? 'course, they're both off at college now, so it's fine! But..."
*Chapter V.*

"Didn't turn it off, it died. I forgot to charge it, y'know... something about today being the anniversary of... well, y'know? Besides, thought I made it clear I wanted to be alone. And my blood's find, that's why I'm sat down. Just took a correction dose, waiting for it to work."
*Jamie immediately reaches for him, still sniffling.*

Keeley: *steps into the nursery with a radiant smile, stretching her arms wide.* "Oh, come here, my fabulous little prince! Give Mama a huge hug."

Narrator: *Roy carefully shifts Jamie into Keeley's arms, keeping a supportive hand on the small of his back until he is sure his son is securely held against Keeley's chest.*

Roy: *crosses his arms, watching them with a deep, fond scowl.* "Traitor. I literally just promised to tackle a phantom dog into a fence for you, and you ditch me the second she shows up."

Keeley: *presses a loud, dramatic kiss against Jamie's cheek, making a big popping sound.* "Don't listen to him, darling. Your Dada loves his big heroic speeches, but Mama's got the morning snuggles. Are you alright now, sweet boy? No more scary doggies?"

Narrator: *The warm sunlight streams fully into the nursery now, catching the bright yellow paint on the walls and the scattered soft toys across the carpet. Roy leans against the baby changing table, reaching out with one thick finger to gently poke Jamie's stomach.*

Roy: "Right. Enough crying about shit dogs. It's Saturday. That means Uncle Ted's coming over later with those pink biscuits, and if you don't eat your porridge first, I'm giving your share to the birds."

Keeley: *glares at Roy playfully over Jamie's shoulder.* "Roy! We are not threatening his biscuit privileges at six thirty-five in the morning! Besides, Uncle Jamie said he was dropping off a surprise this morning too."

Roy: *lets out a low, long groan, burying his face in his hand.* "Oh, Jesus. What tacky nonsense did Tartt buy him now?"
*Chapter IV.*
*Me and Ted take our seats.*

Narrator: *It is half past midnight. The front hallway is silent except for the low draft filtering past the piece of cardboard and blue painter's tape hastily fixed over the shattered pane of the front door. The chicken parmesan on the dining table has been cleared away untouched.*

Narrator: *In the dimly lit living room, Jake and Amy sit on the couch. The anger, the frustration over missed binders, and the strict parental arguments from earlier have completely evaporated, replaced by a hollow, sickening quiet.*

Amy: *looks down at her phone for the hundredth time, the screen glowing against her tired face.* "Still no location ping. His phone is off. I tried tracking his watch, but he left it charging on his nightstand."

Jake: *stares blankly toward the taped-up front door, his arms resting heavy on his knees.* "He's stayed out late before, Ames... but not like this. Not angry. Not thinking that... that we lied to him his whole life."

Amy: *wipes a stray tear from her cheek, her voice dropping to a fragile whisper.* "We did lie to him, Jake. We kept waiting for the perfect time, the right age, the perfect conversation... and instead he had to read a punishment Punnett square in a high school classroom."

Jake: *turns to her, his expression entirely devoid of his usual joke-making defense mechanism.* "We're going to fix this. When he walks through that door — whenever he walks through that door — we don't yell, we don't lecture, we don't explain away five hours of panic. We just tell him we love him. We answer every single question he has, no matter how much it hurts."

Narrator: *A soft footstep creaks on the wooden stoop outside, followed by the quiet click of a key entering the front lock.*

"Mom, really? You don't remember McGonagall telling you, when I got my letter at 11, that the Decree was binned off after Voldemort's death via Harry in 1998? Or the many times I've performed spells every other summer. Relax..." *I chuckle.*
Chapter I.

messages.content: *Meanwhile, Jamie is already about two blocks away. Despite what his parents think, what he tells them, he's been struggling. He's been feeling really cooped up, hates that stuff like the museum this morning is a regular occurrence. He stops by a nearby cornershop, buys a drink and leave. When he leaves the owner calls the police, recognising who he is.*

*We flashback five years, to the day I had my trial with Richmond, when I was 16. Aunt Becca is sat in the stands with my Mum Alice, her sister, and my Dad, Alex. Becca is reassuring Mum and Dad that if I am signed, it's not because of nepotism.*

Narrator: *The floodlights of Nelson Road beat down on the pitch as the second half intensity ramps up. In the 57th minute, Jan Maas intercepts a sloppy Palace pass and immediately pings a crisp, flat ball out to the left flank.*

Narrator: *James takes it in stride, his first touch glued to his boot. He drops his shoulder, completely selling the first Palace midfielder down the river. A lightning-fast step-over leaves the second defender tangled in his own feet. As the third man lunges in desperately, James simply rolls the ball back with his studs and pivots, suddenly finding himself with a clear, glorious sight of the goal. The stadium collectively inhales, the Richmond faithful ready to erupt for the hat-trick.*

Narrator: *Instead, James glances up. He spots the blur of a Richmond kit sprinting into the space behind the defense.*

Narrator: *The cross is an absolute peach—a perfectly weighted, curling delivery that bypasses the frantic Palace center-backs entirely. It drops beautifully toward the far post, right into the path of the sprinting striker.*

Narrator: *Dani Rojas doesn't even need to break his stride. He meets the ball perfectly in the air, hammering a thunderous volley past the stranded keeper and into the roof of the net. 3-1.*

Dani: *sprints toward James with his arms thrown wide open, his magnificent hair bouncing wildly with every step.* "Football is life! And Jimmy is life! Muchas gracias, mi hermano!" *leaps into the air, wrapping James in a massive, crushing hug.* "What a pass! Like a gift from the heavens!"

The rest of the team swarms them near the corner flag, a chaotic pile of joyous pushing and shouting.

Jamie: *jogs over and smacks James on the back of the head, a massive grin on his face.* "Oi! That was actually decent, that. Very mature of you, giving up the hat-trick. I would've shot it, obviously, because I'm a striker and I have a sickness, but good on you, mate."

Narrator: *Down on the touchline, the coaching staff reacts with matching enthusiasm.*

Ted: *beams, pointing dual finger-guns toward the pitch.* "Now that is what I call sharing the wealth, Coach! The boy could've gone for personal glory, but he chose the team. You love to see it."

Beard: *nods slowly, his eyes narrowing in approval as he jots something down on his clipboard.* "The assist is the most noble of all statistics. It is the socialist ideal made manifest on the pitch."

Roy: *stands at the edge of his technical area, giving a single, firm clap of his hands.* "Good! That's exactly what I meant! Look at Henderson, he's ready to cry!"
*Chapter VII.*
*It's a Saturday morning. Jake and Amy are in the kitchen of their suburban house, sat around the kitchen table eating breakfast. It's currently 10am. Jamie is still fast asleep in bed upstairs.*
"No... sleep. Don' want to..." *I mumble.* "Scared..."
*The four of them wait for Jamie at the terminal, when they arrive at JFK a few moments later. He's still about 45 minutes away, not landed yet.*

*By the time Mama gets me to the kitchen Dada has already got the Nuggies on. I wiggle out of Mama's arms, toddling over to the oven and pressing my hands and nose to the door.* "Mhmmm... Nuggies." *I giggle.*

Narrator: *The moment James pushes through the double doors of the boot room, the usual Monday morning chatter dies an instant death. It takes exactly three seconds for the swarm to form. The UK sports press clearly caught wind of the leak, and the locker room is practically vibrating with the news.*

Jan: *adjusts the strap of his duffel bag.* "I read the reports this morning. Statistically, going to Tottenham is a very poor career choice if you actually wish to win trophies."

Colin: *winces and shakes his head.* "Jesus, Jan. Ease him in, yeah?"

Jamie: *steps right to the front of the pack, looking genuinely put out.* "It's bollocks though, right, Jimmy? Tell me it's bollocks. You can't fuck off to North London. We're a double act. Who's gonna hit me on the volley when I make my run? You're my guy."

Dani: *clutches his hands to his chest, looking deeply distressed.* "Richmond is your family, James! You cannot leave your family for a bird on a basketball!"

Isaac: *crosses his massive arms, his expression unreadable and imposing.* "Captains don't let their CAMs just walk away. We ain't done building this team."

Narrator: *Before the wall of players can press in any closer, a harsh, gravelly bark cuts through the noise from the far side of the room.*

Roy: *shoves his way aggressively through the center of the players.* "Oi! Back the fuck off!"

Narrator: *The players immediately take a collective half-step back, though they don't disperse completely. Roy stops right in front of James, his expression a thunderous, terrifying scowl.*

Roy: *points a single, threatening finger at the assembled team.* "If any of you muppets asks him about this again before training, I will make you run laps until your hamstrings snap like dry spaghetti. Get your boots on and get out on the pitch. Now."

The team scatters almost instantly, grabbing their gear with rushed murmurs.

Roy: *turns his glare back to James, his voice dropping into a low, private growl.* "Coach's office. Right fucking now."

*Appearing at that moment there is a man and woman, Callum's parents. They missed the assault and have no idea what happened. When Jake and Amy explain through anger and gritted teeth, Callum's mom is nearly sick.*

Narrator: *The sheer, frantic spike of adrenaline gives Jamie just enough strength to shove them away. Jake instantly opens his hands and lets go, choosing to throw his arms up in a gesture of surrender rather than risk bruising Jamie's wrists or wrestling with a boy who has three broken ribs. Amy gasps softly, quickly pulling her hands back to her chest and taking a hurried step backward.*

Jake: *takes another deliberate step back from the bed, keeping his hands raised where Jamie can see them.* "Okay. Okay, we're stopping. Everyone stop. Just breathe, buddy. We're backing up. You have space."

Amy: *swallows hard, forcing her trembling voice into the calmest register she can manage.* "We're not touching you, Jamie. We're stepping back. Just... please, please try not to move your right leg."

Narrator: *The sudden, violent exertion of shouting and shoving immediately demands a toll. Without the heavy flow of painkillers, the three fractured ribs scream in protest, seizing like a vice around Jamie's chest and making it agonizingly difficult to pull in the oxygen his lungs desperately need. The monitors on the wall blare a frantic, high-pitched warning as his heart rate spikes. His vocal cords, scraped completely raw by the breathing tube, burn with every ragged, shallow gasp.*

Dr. Lin: *keeps the gauze pressed firmly against the bleeding crook of Jamie's right arm, his tone even but strictly professional.* "Jamie, listen to me. I am Dr. Lin. I am backing up as much as I can, but you just pulled out your fentanyl line. Your body has been through massive trauma, and you are going to be in an excruciating amount of pain in about thirty seconds. I need you to let Nurse Park establish a new IV in your left hand. We are not going to crowd you, but you have to let us help the pain."

Nurse Park stands frozen at the foot of the bed with a fresh IV kit, waiting for Jamie to give the slightest indication of compliance. Over by the heavy double doors, Mac has instinctively wrapped his arms around Ellie, pulling his little sister against his side. They stare in wide-eyed terror at their older cousin, watching the absolute agony and devastation rip through him as the adrenaline begins to fade and the agonizing reality of the room crashes back in.

Narrator: *Outside the carriage window, the late afternoon sun has given way to the deep purple twilight of the Scottish Highlands. The long hours on the train had blurred into a haze of sweet wrappers, shared secrets, ridiculous memories of their first four years, and a few quiet, emotional moments over missing home and the mounting pressure of their fifth year.*

Isobel: *dabs at the corner of her eye with her sleeve, letting out a lingering, half-amused breath as she looks down at the pile of empty Pumpkin Pasty wrappers between them.* "I still can't believe we both started crying over our first-year Flying lesson. You almost dove headfirst into the Herbology greenhouse, Peralta. That wasn't a heartwarming memory — that was almost an absolute disaster!"

Jamie: *grins, adjusting his glasses as he stands up to pull his dark Hogwarts robes over his shoulders.* "Hey, that was a legendary recovery, and Professor Abbot said the cabbages were barely damaged! Besides, you cried first when we were talking about missing Brooklyn street food."

Isobel: *scoffs playfully, buttoning her Gryffindor cloak with practiced ease.* "I got emotional about the garlic knots from that place near your dad's precinct! There is a huge difference, Peralta. That's real, deep-seated cultural grief."

Narrator: *The train brakes begin to squeal with a sharp metallic hiss that echoes down the entire length of the Hogwarts Express. Outside, the familiar oil lamps of Hogsmeade Station flicker through the gathering mist, casting golden pools of light across the dark, crowded wooden platform.*

Jamie: *slings his satchel over his shoulder, looking across at his best friend with a sense of calm that had completely replaced his nervous energy on the platform.* "Ready for year five, Izzie?"

Isobel: *gives his shoulder a quick, solid nudge as she slides open the compartment door into the noisy corridor.* "Ready as I'll ever be. Come on, let me through so we can grab a carriage before the Slytherins claim all the good ones."

*Jamie returns with their drinks, but forgot his own. Grumbling, he reaches for his wand, pointing it into his glass.* "Aguamenti..." *The glass fills up alright... a little too much. Jake and Amy laugh, Jamie stares at the glass and his wand for a moment, then bursts out laughing as well, soaked.*

Narrator:
The holding cell is silent save for the ragged, shuddering breaths of the three of them held tight on the cold concrete floor. The six months of absolute terror and cold silence seem to concentrate into this single, crushing moment as Jamie buries his face deeper into the worn leather of his father's coat.

Jamie:
*He clings weakly to the fabric of Jake's jacket, his voice coming out as a tiny, strained raspy whisper.*
"They... they hurt me..."

Narrator:
Hearing his voice for the first time in half a year—cracked, broken, and filled with deep exhaustion—strikes Jake and Amy like a physical blow.

Jake:
*He tightens his arms around Jamie, holding his head gently against his neck as tears soak into his shirt.*
"I know, buddy. I know. I'm so, so sorry. But it's over now, Jamie. Nobody is ever going to touch you again. I swear to you, I will never let anyone hurt you ever again."

Amy:
*She presses her face against Jamie's shoulder, running a trembling hand gently over his back.*
"You're safe with us now, sweetie. Mom's got you. Dad's got you. We're taking you home."
Chapter I.
*Becca nods, understanding it. Her hand slides to Rosa, under her waistband and finds her clit, rubbing soft circles with her index finger and thumb.*

Amy: *types away on her phone screen with a soft smirk.* "I told him yes, but only if he gets a slice of garlic knot crust for the house on his way back. And I reminded him about his curfew."

Jake: *points an finger at her.* "Good call on the garlic knots. That's high-level tactical parenting right there. You know, seeing him just be a kid... it makes me feel a lot better about the whole magic thing."

Amy: *sets her phone back down on the kitchen counter and walks over to the living room, leaning against the arm of the couch.*

Amy: *softens her expression as she looks over at Jake.* "What do you mean?"

Jake: *tosses the baseball up in the air once more and catches it cleanly.* "I don't know, Ames. Sometimes when he's talking about O.W.L.s and Human Transfiguration and all those crazy ancient laws, it feels like he's growing up in a world that's millions of miles away from us. But then he texts you a picture of an arcade high score, and he's still just Jamie from Brooklyn."

Amy: *smiles gently, resting her hand on Jake's shoulder.* "He'll always be Jamie from Brooklyn, Jake. No matter how much magic he learns, or how many spells he masters... he's got too much of both of us in him to ever lose that."

Narrator: *The Peralta-Santiago kitchen is warm, chaotic, and smells heavily of garlic. The dining table is covered in the remnants of Friday night Italian takeout, a long-standing tradition that Amy only allows because she meticulously balances the family's nutritional macros over the rest of the week.*

Jake: *leans forward over his paper plate.* "And that is exactly why you never trust a guy who says he 'only steals artisanal cheeses.' It's a gateway crime, Mac. First it's a wedge of smoked gouda, next thing you know, you're fencing stolen Fabergé eggs in a warehouse down by the docks."

Amy: *wipes a smudge of tomato sauce off the table.* "He stole three blocks of sharp cheddar from a corner bodega, Jake. It wasn't exactly a high-stakes heist. And he surrendered the second you tripped over the mop bucket."

Jake: *points a plastic fork defensively.* "I didn't trip, I executed a tactical stumble to lower my center of gravity. And the point is, the Dairy Desperado is finally off the streets."

Ellie: *kicks her legs under the table.* "That's a terrible villain name, Dad. You should have called him the Cheese Thief. It has a better ring to it."

Mac: *looks up from his phone screen.* "Cheese and thief don't rhyme, El. Anyway, Jamie just texted in the group chat. Uncle Mark tried to make Chicago deep-dish from scratch again and set off the smoke alarms. They're ordering pizza."

Amy: *shakes her head with a fond sigh.* "I love Mark, I really do, but Alice needs to ban him from the oven. Did Jamie say if they've booked their flights for the summer yet? Because I've already started outlining the logistical parameters for this year's family puzzle-hunt."

Jake: *gasps dramatically.* "You started without me? Ames, we agreed this was the year we completely and utterly crush the boys. Jamie is getting way too smart. He's practically a fifteen-year-old cyber-hacker now, and Mac is his inside man. We need to bring our absolute A-game."

Mac: *grins and reaches for a leftover garlic knot.* "You guys are going down this year. Jamie and I have been strategizing since Christmas."
*Chapter II.*

The great doors of Dragonsreach swing open, and the Captain of the Guard strides into the hall, his face a grim thundercloud. The usual low murmur of the court quiets as he approaches the throne. Jarl Balgruuf the Greater watches him come, his hand resting on the arm of his throne, his expression shifting from mild curiosity to concern. Proventus Avenicci adjusts his fine robes nervously, while the Dunmer housecarl, Irileth, straightens, her hand instinctively moving closer to the hilt of her sword.
Jarl Balgruuf: "Captain. Your face tells a story I'm not certain I want to hear. Report."
Captain: *He stops before the dais and gives a curt bow.* "My Jarl. There has been an attack. In the dungeons."
Irileth: *Her voice is sharp, cutting through the hall.* "An attack? How?"
Captain: "Magic, my Jarl. A guard, Thorgar, is dead. He was... disintegrated. Reduced to a pile of ash."
Farengar Secret-Fire: *The court wizard, who had been examining a tome nearby, looks up, his eyes alight with intense, almost predatory, curiosity.* "Disintegrated, you say? Utterly? What was the residual energy signature? Arcane? Elemental?"
Jarl Balgruuf: *He holds up a hand, silencing his wizard.* "Later, Farengar. Continue, Captain. Who is responsible?"
Captain: "We don't know, my Jarl. There was no sign of an intruder. The Breton noble, Lord Frey, was also a victim. The blast seems to have originated near his cell. He was knocked unconscious and sustained a wound to his arm. We found his blood on the stone. He's with the healers now."
Proventus Avenicci: "The noble from Daggerfall? Attacked in our cells? Jarl, this is a diplomatic catastrophe!"
Captain: "He appears to be the only witness. He's badly shaken, but coherent. He has demanded an audience with you personally as soon as his wounds are treated."
Jarl Balgruuf: *His eyes narrow, a dangerous look hardening his features.* "An unknown mage attacks my dungeon, murders one of my guards, and assaults a noble guest under my roof... He will have his audience. Irileth, I want the keep on high alert. Double the patrols. Farengar, go. See what you can learn from that ash. Captain, as soon as Lord Frey is able, bring him to me."

Narrator: *The quiet, rhythmic ticking of the grandfather clock is violently shattered by the shrill, deafening wail of the ambulance siren. The warm, dimly lit memory of the foyer dissolves into the harsh, clinical fluorescence of the emergency rig.*

Narrator: *The heavy vibration of the road rumbles through the mattress beneath James's spine. His chest still aches with a deep, crushing pressure, and the cool hiss of the oxygen flowing into his mask is the loudest sound inside the back of the ambulance.*

Rebecca: *is sitting in the exact same position, gripping his hand like it's a lifeline. Her thumb rhythmically strokes across his knuckles, her eyes fiercely locked onto his pale face.* "I'm still right here, James. I've got you."

Paramedic: *braces himself against the wall as the ambulance takes a final, sharp turn, reaching up to tap the radio clipped to his shoulder.* "Control, this is Alpha-Seven. We are two minutes out from St. George's. Patient is a twenty-one-year-old male, post-cardiac event, currently conscious but tachycardic. Have the Resus team standing by."

Narrator: *The radio crackles with a brief confirmation. The paramedic looks down at James, offering a tight, professional nod of encouragement.*

Paramedic: *checks the IV line taped to the back of James's hand.* "Almost there, mate. You've done brilliantly. Just hang on for two more minutes and we'll have you properly sorted."

Narrator: *Through the small, frosted windows in the rear doors, the bright afternoon sunlight flickers as the ambulance turns off the main road and begins its rapid descent toward the emergency drop-off bay of St. George's Hospital. The engine downshifts, the siren cutting out abruptly as they enter the hospital grounds, leaving only the urgent, rapid beeping of James's heart monitor filling the silence.*
*We then skip forward, to 3 years after my tryout. I'm 19, me and Becca are just getting home to her house, after my parents funeral.*

Narrator: *Captain Miller holds the folded flag out with rigid precision. The entire bullpen stands frozen in a heavy, suffocating silence.*

Rosa: *reaches out with shaking hands and takes the flag, pressing it tight against her chest as a choked sob breaks from her throat.*

Narrator: *Her knees give out beneath her. Terry and Jake move in an instant, catching her on either side before she hits the floor and carefully guiding her into a chair. Charles quietly hurries into Holt's office, wiping his eyes with his sleeve to grab a glass of water.*

Jake: *kneels beside Rosa's chair, tears welling in his eyes as his voice cracks.* "We've got you, Rosa. We've got you, okay? We're right here."

Holt: *steps forward, placing a steady hand on Captain Miller's arm and speaking in a low, somber tone.* "Thank you, Captain. We will ensure Detective Diaz and her family have everything they require. The NYPD will take it from here."
